entries.en:
The second volume of the hugely popular epic novel 'The Tale of the Last Sword,' 'The Pitch-Black Chapter,' has been released. This time, the setting changes completely from the first volume, and the story quite literally ventures into pitch-black darkness.
With just its first two volumes published, the series already conveys an epic scale.
Its author, O. R. James, said: 'I have planned out all ten volumes. Now the characters should weave the story themselves.'
We eagerly await volume three and beyond.

Late tonight, a mysterious black life-form that appeared on Nanohana Street in Miyato City was repelled by a gigantic humanoid weapon that emerged from the road. A government announcement also established that this mysterious life-form will be called an 'Angel.'

The Angel had been destroying nearby buildings, but the gigantic humanoid weapon prevented further damage.
No detailed information about this humanoid weapon is currently available.

entries.en:
Late tonight, an attack by the Angel that appeared on Nanohana Street in Miyato City caused a tanker truck parked on the road to explode, setting the area ablaze.
The Angel was fighting a gigantic humanoid weapon that had emerged from the road, and a stray shot is believed to have struck the tanker. The truck carried gasoline and diesel fuel and was on its way to nearby gas stations. Its driver and local residents had evacuated, and there appear to be no casualties from the explosion.

Local residents say they knew the equipment had been installed, but did not know what it was for.

entries.en:
Some information that is hard to believe has reached us, and I would like to share it.
If you looked at the houseplant in this photograph and wondered why no one had picked it up, you had the same thought I did.
In fact, it was not knocked over by an earthquake or an accident. It was deliberately laid on its side.
Research claims that a houseplant laid on its side produces ten times the usual amount of the relaxing substance 'shinotony,' and the practice is reportedly spreading gradually through offices.
Interviews at offices trying it revealed substantial effects: 'It felt strange at first, and I doubted it would work, but our business performance improved by 10 percent,' and 'People's expressions softened, and communication in the office became smoother.'
The research institution behind the findings explained: 'Just as people relax when they lie down, we discovered that plants also relax more on their sides, which stimulates their production of shinotony.' I have already begun trying it in my own office and hope to report the results next time.

entries.en:
I spoke to a woman who had not fled, but was keeping her station kiosk open as usual while giant creatures rampaged right nearby.
'This seems to be the only shop still open...' Something sounded caught in her throat, so I pressed her for more.
Her answer was dispiriting: 'The higher-ups told us not to close. They said it would make an inspiring story and raise the share price.' She continued: 'They say they'll fire me if I close. They'll blacklist me so I can't get another job... Of course, my life matters, so I do plan to run if things get really bad.'
Having said this, the woman smiled as if a weight had lifted. Then she added: 'Now that I've said it, I'll be fired. But I feel better. Put it in your article. It's the truth.'
This article may cost her her job. But as the person publishing it, I want to help her too. Together with the contents of the USB drive she gave me at the end, I plan to expose the company's dark side in our next report.

entries.en:
Inside a building right beside where the giant creatures appeared, people were still buried in work.
As a giant creature struck the building, windows shattered, walls cracked, and office papers scattered everywhere. Yet they calmly continued working as though nothing had happened. The sight was both sublime and horrifying.
When I tried to visit the office later, the building had been declared off-limits because it was at risk of collapse.
I could not reach its management either, and still do not know whether those people escaped safely.
When I visited the building, I thought I faintly heard the tapping of keyboards drifting down from an upper floor on the wind. I can only pray that I imagined it.

entries.en:
An office reportedly received a mysterious fax late one night.
It read 'B E H I N D' in letters that looked as though they had been written with a finger dipped in liquid.
Another fax arrived at the same time the following day. The message was identical, but apparently it had been written anew, as the letters differed slightly.
These mysterious faxes continued for two weeks.
Unable to ignore them any longer, the office consulted the police, who would not take the matter seriously. With no other choice, they hired a detective to investigate the sender.
The sender's number was soon identified, but it had not been used in decades, and its former owner was already dead. The detective also found the site of the former owner's home, but it was apparently an abandoned house.

There proved to be no connection whatsoever between the office staff and the former owner or their relatives.
The faxes kept arriving every day while the detective investigated, even after the office switched to a new fax number.
When that fax alone continued to arrive despite the machine being unplugged, they could no longer believe an ordinary living person was responsible.

Why was it being sent, by whom, how, and for what purpose?
'I've solved the mystery. It's...' The detective's telephone report broke off there, and the detective has been missing ever since.
Several more detectives were hired afterward, but each disappeared just as they seemed to reach the answer. Word of this spread, and apparently no detective will take the case now.

At the office, the fax still arrives at the same time every day.

entries.en:
Stacks of meticulously filed documents pack the office shelves. It is a familiar sight to working adults, especially those known as white-collar workers.
Despite the spread of computers and the many years since 'paperless' became a buzzword, things still look like this.

Even documents requiring signatures can now be handled with pen tablets and similar devices. Why can we still not move beyond paper?
One theory likens it to the desire to possess things.
There is reassurance in having something physical, paper, rather than something electronic.
People from generations that did not grow up with computers are particularly uneasy about the unfamiliar idea of digitization. Paper, which they can see and touch, makes them feel secure.

I believe there is a place for paper documents that should be preserved, including for sentimental reasons.
Still, I cannot help feeling that far too much unnecessary paper remains.

entries.en:
Office shelves are a common sight, but today I would like to introduce one fitted with the latest newly developed equipment.
First, the space for hanging coats becomes an emergency shelter capsule.
Step inside and press the switch at the back, and a shutter lowers to seal you off from the outside.
It is waterproof, so water cannot enter. Various devices are built into the shelving frame, one of which purifies outside air and sends it inside. Remarkably, it can even generate air when surrounded by seawater.
Naturally, it also includes a simple toilet and air conditioning to prevent odors from lingering.
A monitor shows your surroundings through the shelf's cameras and sensors, as well as high-resolution images from a dedicated satellite.
Because the satellite monitors your situation, a specialized rescue team will rush to you if, for example, you are buried under rubble or submerged in water.

I can only marvel at how far technology has come.

entries.en:
Water dispensers provide clean drinking water whenever you want it. They are now widely used in offices and homes.
But is that water really safe?
A company was investigated last week. The story received little attention, overshadowed by a political scandal around the same time, but this supplier was filling tanks with tap water and selling it as 'pure water.'
Worse, it added the disinfectant calcium hypochlorite as a precaution, then mixed in a compound called Monefurio to mask the smell.

That was not all. The water tanks were discarded, deteriorated containers from other suppliers that it collected without permission and reused.

And the tap water came from public facilities such as parks in the dead of night. It leaves me speechless.

Is the company supplying your water dispenser trustworthy?
I recommend checking the list of companies whose safety has been confirmed on the Consumer Affairs Agency website.

entries.en:
The red button above a fire hydrant. Everyone knows it sounds an emergency alarm when pressed.
And yet, how many of us feel tempted to press it when we see it? Of course, pressing it when there is no emergency is nothing but a nuisance. Even adults who know this may suddenly feel the urge when it catches their eye.
Research has reportedly linked this to stress. The more stressed someone is, the more readily they feel the urge to press it. They want the release of doing something forbidden, or of watching other people panic.
On the other hand, there is an urban legend that it emits radio waves designed to attract attention and arouse curiosity.
The idea is so implausible that no one takes it seriously, and dismantling the device revealed nothing of the sort. The manufacturer and retailer naturally deny it too.
Still, something bothers me. While visiting a company that makes fire hydrants, I happened to glimpse inside a warehouse storing finished units and thought I saw something like an altar. The warehouse door was quickly closed, but the employee accompanying me seemed to tense up for an instant.
I will continue investigating. Please await further reports.

entries.en:
These cardboard boxes are piled across an office corridor.
They are reportedly full of office documents and have been left like this because there is nowhere to put them.
Seeing such a scene deeply saddens me, because it sharply reduces these workers' chances of surviving a disaster.

In my reporting, I have confirmed several cases where piles of documents prevented people from reaching emergency stairs, or where falling boxes crushed people to death.

You need not tidy up just to make things look nice. Please do it to help yourself survive.

entries.en:
A malicious crime involving an AED has occurred.
A young passerby used an AED on an elderly man who collapsed with respiratory failure, but sadly the man could not be saved.
A member of the public is not held criminally responsible merely because their use of an AED in an emergency fails to save someone.
So what was the problem?
In fact, it was a crime the young person had planned.
Noticing the elderly stranger's considerable assets, the culprit began by exchanging greetings in parks as though by chance, eventually winning his trust as if they were his own grandchild.
With no family, the elderly man believed the lies, adopted the young person, and arranged for them to receive a substantial insurance payout if anything happened to him.
The culprit then gradually weakened him by mixing drugs into his tea and other drinks.
That was what caused the man to collapse in the street.
Terrifyingly, the culprit also seems to have tampered with the AED when using it.

Given the circumstances of the man's death, no particular investigation was conducted, and the plot seemed to have succeeded.
How was it exposed?
The truth is revealed in 'A Collection of Miraculous Mysteries: Modern Sentiments,' now on sale to great acclaim.

entries.en:
Did you know that an ordinary station ticket machine conceals a unique trick?
Choose certain buttons in a particular order and rhythm, and it will issue a special ticket.

The special ticket cannot be used for travel, but hand it to a station employee and you will receive something in return.

Unfortunately, I cannot reveal exactly how to perform the trick, or what you receive, here.
However, I really did obtain the special ticket, and what I received in exchange made my life considerably richer.
If you manage to get that special ticket, there is no doubt that it will bring happiness to anyone.

entries.en:
A man was seen photographing a giant creature from close by.
He reportedly climbed onto an abandoned car and filmed intently while the creature's huge tail passed right overhead.

We learned that he was a freelance photographer, but even given his profession, one must question such a dangerous act.
When I managed to contact him later, I put that question to him.
'There are things only I can do. That's all.' With those words, he headed for his next assignment.
Photographers and journalists seem to have a stronger resolve than I imagined.
Still, I believe it is also necessary to avoid danger when the situation demands it.
Once you lose your life, all is lost.

entries.en:
A man fidgets endlessly outside a public restroom with a 'Cleaning in Progress' sign.
Many of us have encountered this situation: though you rarely use it, you suddenly need a restroom, only to find it being cleaned.
You wonder why it had to happen now. Going to another public restroom would be dangerous, so you tell yourself the cleaning will be over soon and simply keep waiting.
Statistics suggest that people who do this are highly likely to end up having to search for another restroom anyway.
This is because cleaning a restroom takes far more effort and time than you might imagine.
With that in mind, it is wiser to look elsewhere as soon as you learn the restroom is being cleaned.
These days, apps can show usable public restrooms near your location. I recommend trying one.

entries.en:
Almost all of them are expressionless.
They neither fawn over customers nor condescendingly suggest they will buy something only because you are in trouble.
They always remain composed.
They would not tell me the details, but apparently the company drills this mindset into them during training.
There is even an urban legend that they are clones, since every employee seems identical in everything, not just clothing. That too apparently results from their training.
And you can see their hidden passion in their eyes. They shine with the conviction that making customers happy by buying their goods is their own greatest joy.

entries.en:
Our popular 'Tipsy Sightseeing' series, written under the inspiration of a pleasant buzz, has reached its 10,482nd installment.

This time, we are looking at emergency stairs.
When you are tipsy, resting your cheek against a step feels wonderfully cool.
They are also ideal for quietly crouching down when you feel low.
If the emergency stairs are outdoors rather than enclosed by walls, they can even serve as a kitchen for grilling dried fish during late-night overtime.

Be aware that, especially overseas, doors on emergency stairs sometimes cannot be opened from the stairwell except on the first floor for security reasons.
Take care not to step into a high-rise stairwell by mistake and find yourself forced to descend an absurd number of floors.

entries.en:
Late at night, the tapping of a keyboard echoes through a dim office.
A man is working alone.
He founded the company and now runs it by himself. As usual, he is typing relentlessly, this time to meet a deadline the following morning.
Apparently, this situation is almost constant. He rarely returns to his apartment, and bathes and does his laundry at nearby facilities.
He says he enjoys his work, but should such working conditions really be left unchallenged?
I know that being able to do as much of the work you love as you want may sound enviable to many people. Still, I cannot help wondering whether it is healthy for a living creature, for a human being.

entries.en:
A woman crouches in a dim office.
Speak to her, and she mutters something before moving away, still crouching.
It seems impossible demands at work have caused her stress to erupt in this form.
There were other employees around, but no one tried to calm or comfort her. None of them had the spare energy.

It should have been a deeply sad sight.
But I happened to learn later that this woman was a difficult employee who crouched down in protest over the slightest thing.
She routinely forgot to report things or neglected assigned tasks because she did not know how to proceed. When someone pointed this out, she behaved in the same way.
I could not hide my astonishment at behavior as childish as a small child throwing a tantrum in a toy shop.

More frightening still, apparently the number of adults who behave like this is rising rapidly.

entries.en:
Few people realize that getting out of a stopped car to inspect the situation during a sudden incident can itself be dangerous.
On highways and ordinary roads alike, as long as cars and motorcycles are moving, standing carelessly in the roadway puts you at risk of being struck by approaching traffic.

It is understandable to panic when placed in circumstances most people would never encounter in a lifetime.
But it is precisely at such times that everyday precautions can help you avoid an unexpected accident.

In reality, we often only notice this when it happens to us. I hope this article can serve as a lesson and help as many people as possible.

entries.en:
People flee, trying to avoid falling rubble from collapsing buildings.
As with disasters such as earthquakes, it is important to stay somewhere as safe as possible from a collapse.
On a broad street like this one, the central divider is one example. There is no danger there of being struck by approaching traffic either.

It is important to understand that all kinds of objects can become deadly hazards, and to think through such situations in advance.

entries.en:
Amid all this chaos, one woman stayed inside the station rather than fleeing.
She was waiting for the man she had been dating for about three years.
Unable to contact him because of the disturbances, she had also lost one of the earrings he gave her on their first date,
and dropped the matching watch they had bought together.
Despite one ominous event after another, she simply waited.
Perhaps she did not want to show her devotion. She deliberately acted irritated and complained about her boyfriend's shortcomings.
Trembling with fear, she nevertheless bravely kept waiting.
The fleeting expression on her face when her boyfriend finally reached the station said more than anything else could.
Quickly hiding it, she cursed at him as the two left the danger zone together.

With so much grim news during these incidents, I would like to thank this couple for giving us such a heartwarming sight.
